subject: Re: Access to annotations audit trail (actions/timestamps/values)
text:
Hi Seif,

Many Thanks for this recommendation from the Encord team. I think it would be important to find a way to keep an appropriate backup of the deleted/edited values in Encord, to comply with the requirement (i.e. this is probably a more consistent way than the current data-backups solution we've implemented).

What do you mean precisely by creating a "label branch"?

(In general terms) does the team mean e.g.:
- for a "nodule" keypoint term, in the same project's ontology, we would create a corresponding "nodule_backup" keypoing term (the "label branch"),
and create a script to copy the nodule keypoints labels and attribute values into a new "nodule_backup keypoint", when submitting a task?
- Every time a "nodule" keypoint attribute is changed, we would again create a new "nodule_backup keypoint", copying all the previous info + the new change?
- (Assuming there is no way to hide the "label branch" in the ontology) - we would need to convey to the users, which terms are used to
label, and which terms are not; and in case the tasks are re-opened, which labels can be re-edited and which cannot be?

This last point would create some contention, as we would try to avoid confusing the users, so if there is a way to keep the "label branch"
(ontology term and respective labels, or at least just the latter) hidden from the annotation interface, we would be happy to hear about it.

In case I've misinterpret, could the team please provide an example?

Many Thanks,
Best Wishes
Mauro

Dr. Mauro Santos

Research Scientist

Optellum Ltd. www.optellum.com<http://www.optellum.com/>

subject: Re: Updated invitation with note: Encord <> Deep Health | Product Alignment & Next steps @ Tue 18 Mar 2025 10am - 10:30am (GMT) (jim.tol@deephealth.co
text:
Hi Leo, Kamil,

As promised, find attached a video on how our prostate software visualizes a 4D (DCE) scan.
In the first 3 seconds, we scroll through the slices of the 4D image. You can see in the top-right corner that only the z-index changes.
Afterwards, we pause on a specific slice (z-index 10) and scroll through the timepoints. You can see that only the last coordinate (T) changes. In all, there are 45 different timepoints.
What the radiologist is interested in seeing is the earlier uptake of the contrast agent in the lesion (orange ROI) compared to the rest of the prostate. Around timepoint 21, you can see that the lesion is relatively bright compared to the rest of the prostate. This is indicative of malignancy.

Hope this clarifies what we are looking for in terms of 4D image support.

Also, I reached out to my colleagues regarding datasets to share. One of them informed me that Julie Sheffield already shared 4 Mammo datasets with Kamil back in September. Do you still have those on hand? We would be keen to use these datasets for testing again.

Many thanks,
Jim

text:
Hi Shivant,

Unfortunately, we’ll not be able to make it for a call, as we’re extremely busy this period, and we’ve finalised our decision to move to another platform.

Here is some feedback regarding our experience with Encord:

Positives:

  *   Induction process
  *   Keeping up to date with current foundation models and quick integration on the platform
  *   Data curation features on the web UI
  *   Good documentation
Negatives:

  *   Basic features were missing, compared to other platforms, or have been introduced recently
  *   Lots of bugs early on made the process not easy to get up to speed
  *   Not having a trial period with the platform
  *   Cost

I hope the above is useful to you.

Thanks,
Kostas

I'm finding that every episode I've reviewed where more than one object is
collected has the high-level classification labeled incorrectly.  The
timestamps seem mostly fine.  I'm wondering if, rather than
rejecting/re-opening all of these, we write a script on our end to replace
these label strings with the correct one so that we don't lose the
annotation time.  To put it another way: I would want the annotators to use
the correct label going forward, but we would knowingly approve past,
incorrect ones with the plan to replace them on our end.

Evan
